patterns.message: Import across projects by package name (@cadastre/x), never by a relative path: a relative path escaping its project is invisible to the boundary rules below, which match on package names (ADR-0006).

A context (type:context) and the edge (type:edge) may depend only on the published language (@cadastre/api-contracts), the shared kernel (@cadastre/shared) and technical adapters (@cadastre/event-publisher, @cadastre/logger). The way out is the contracts package: route cross-context traffic through it, never through another context's internals (ADR-0006).
Import across projects by package name (@cadastre/x), never by a relative path: a relative path escaping its project is invisible to the boundary rules below, which match on package names (ADR-0006).

Contracts (type:contracts) and technical adapters (type:adapter) may depend only on the shared kernel (@cadastre/shared). The way out is to move what you need into the kernel if its meaning is identical everywhere, or to leave it with its owner if it is not (ADR-0006).
Import across projects by package name (@cadastre/x), never by a relative path: a relative path escaping its project is invisible to the boundary rules below, which match on package names (ADR-0006).

The shared kernel (type:kernel) is the bottom of the stack and depends on nothing in the workspace. The way out is to leave the concept with the context that owns it: if only one context needs it, it is not kernel (ADR-0006).
Import across projects by package name (@cadastre/x), never by a relative path: a relative path escaping its project is invisible to the boundary rules below, which match on package names (ADR-0006).

The domain layer reads without knowing the framework or the ORM: no Nest, no Prisma, and no import from application/, infrastructure/ or presentation/. The way out is to invert it — declare what you need as a port in application/ports and let the use case pass the answer in (ADR-0004).
A context (type:context) may depend only on the published language (@cadastre/api-contracts) and the shared kernel (@cadastre/shared); the domain layer normally needs neither (ADR-0006).
Import across projects by package name (@cadastre/x), never by a relative path: a relative path escaping its project is invisible to the boundary rules below, which match on package names (ADR-0006).

The application layer names ports, not adapters: it may not import infrastructure/ or presentation/. The way out is an abstract class in application/ports bound to its adapter in the module (ADR-0004).

A context (type:context) may depend only on the published language (@cadastre/api-contracts), the shared kernel (@cadastre/shared) and technical adapters (@cadastre/event-publisher, @cadastre/logger) (ADR-0006).
Import across projects by package name (@cadastre/x), never by a relative path: a relative path escaping its project is invisible to the boundary rules below, which match on package names (ADR-0006).

The API client (type:client) speaks the published language and nothing else: it may depend on @cadastre/api-contracts and on no other workspace package. It is what a caller outside the system can reach, so giving it a context's internals would make it prove things no real client could do (ADR-0007).
